info.title: Liquid inference API
info.description:
OpenAI-compatible inference API plus native endpoints.

**Authentication** — Every request needs an API key, sent as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer $LIQUID_API_KEY`. Create a key on the [API keys](https://console.liquid.ai/dashboard/api-keys) page of Liquid Console; it is shown once.

**Batch uploads** — Batch input files are uploaded through a presigned URL from `POST /v1/files`; see the [Batch guide](https://docs.liquid.ai/api/guides/batch).

**Decision models** — `POST /decisions/v1/systemone` answers typed questions using models such as `d1.2` and `d1.2-ultra`.

ChatMessage.description: Role-specific OpenAI-compatible messages. Tool results must use the corresponding tool_call_id. Preserve returned reasoning with an assistant tool-call turn when the model requires it. Earlier spoken replies must be sent as their transcript in content; audio.id alone is not supported.

range.description: Ascending [low, high] interval for estimation. Without range, read a number from the state.

step.description: Requires range and must divide it into equal parts.

DecisionQuestion.description: Named typed question. box and boxes require exactly one image. Instructions are written text or JSON; send audio clips in the request audio array, not as spoken instructions.

path.description: JSON Pointer for a span in a JSON state, when provided.
JSON Pointer for a span in a JSON state, when provided.
JSON Pointer for a span in a JSON state, when provided.
JSON Pointer for a span in a JSON state, when provided.

DecisionAnswer.description: An answer for the question under the same key. Read values are null when found < 0.5. Spans are [start, end) Unicode code-point offsets into the state (JSON states use two-space indentation). Box edges are fractions of the image. Estimate interval is [p10, p90].

Fetch a model your organization can access.

post.description: Generate a model response for a chat conversation. See [Text generation](https://docs.liquid.ai/api/guides/text-generation). Sampling, tool calling, reasoning, and structured output support depend on the selected model. With stream=true the response is text/event-stream, rather than a JSON completion.

message.content: Hello! How can I help you today?

model.description: The model that generated the response.

anyOf.description: Reasoning text when returned by the model/parser.

usage.description: Token counts: { prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens }, plus `cost` in USD when the model is priced. Audio models also report OpenAI's `prompt_tokens_details` and `completion_tokens_details`, whose `audio_tokens` say how much of each total was audio. Some vision models bill each image as a multiple of its tokens, counted in `prompt_tokens` as OpenAI does. Streaming responses report it on the final usage chunk.

schema.description: Server-sent events when stream=true. Each data event is a chat.completion.chunk with choices[].delta (content, reasoning, tool_calls, or audio) and finish_reason. A usage chunk may have an empty choices array. The stream ends with data: [DONE].

messages.description: The conversation so far. Messages follow OpenAI role-specific content requirements. User messages may include `image_url` parts for models that take images, each a base64 `data:` URL or an http(s) URL, and `input_audio` parts (base64 WAV, `format: "wav"`) for models that take audio; other models return 400. Liquid downloads linked images itself before the request reaches the model, from public addresses only, and returns 400 when one cannot be downloaded or is not a PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF image; a request may link up to 8 images, of at most 10 MB each and 20 MB together.

stream.description: When true, tokens stream back as server-sent events.

modalities.description: Output types. ["text", "audio"] asks a model with speech output for a spoken reply, returned in `message.audio` (or streamed in `delta.audio`) beside the text. Defaults to ["text"]; models without speech output return 400.

audio.description: Spoken reply options when `modalities` includes "audio", as in OpenAI: `{ "voice", "format" }`. `format` is `pcm16` (headerless 16-bit PCM, 24 kHz mono), or `wav` (each streamed chunk a complete WAV file); other formats return 400. The reply arrives in `message.audio` or streamed `delta.audio`, with its words in `transcript`. `voice` is accepted but does not change the voice.

voice.description: Accepted for compatibility; does not change the voice.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature; supported values depend on the model.

top_k.description: Top-k sampling, when supported by the model.

max_tokens.description: Maximum generated tokens, including reasoning. Leave enough room for a final answer.

max_completion_tokens.description: OpenAI-compatible output budget; model support may vary. Use one output-budget field per request.

response_format.description: Structured output format, where supported by the selected model.

post.description: Answer named typed questions about text, JSON, images, or audio. Supports noul, choice (including multiple=true), score, text, date, number, box, boxes, and spans. See [Decisions](https://docs.liquid.ai/api/guides/decisions) for examples. The hosted endpoint does not accept video or spoken question instructions; open-weight model APIs have different input shapes.

answers.description: One typed answer per question id, under the same keys.

usage.description: Token counts: { input_tokens, output_tokens }, plus `cost` in USD when the model is priced. `input_tokens` counts the state and images once and each question's own tokens. Output is always 0.

model.description: A decision model id from GET /decisions/v1/models, such as d1.2 or d1.2-ultra. Use the exact id returned for your organization.

state.description: The content the questions are about: plain text, or structured JSON such as a chat log or record. Omit or send null when the questions stand alone. As in Perplexity's Decisions API, an array state may also hold images as OpenAI-style `{ "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "data:…" } }` parts: they are taken out of the state and checked under the same rules as `images`, which the request must then leave out (sending both returns 422), and a single string left beside them becomes the text state.

oneOf.description: Base64 data URL with a matching media content type.

images.description: Up to 8 JPEG, PNG, or WebP images as base64 data URLs or {content_type, base64} objects. Remote URLs are not accepted. Each image is at most 5 MiB, subject to the smaller 4.5 MiB whole-request limit. box and boxes require exactly one image. Check input_modalities in GET /decisions/v1/models for model support.

questions.description: Up to 128 named questions. Each question reads the state and media. d1.2 and d1.2-ultra allow 65,536 input tokens per question and 250,000 bytes of text; the entire request must fit the 4.5 MiB body limit.

oneOf.description: Base64 data URL with a matching media content type.

audio.description: Up to 8 WAV, MP3, FLAC, or OGG clips, at most 300 seconds combined, subject to the whole-request body limit. The declared content type must match the bytes. Check input_modalities for model support. Video is not accepted.
